blocks.text:
Day 3 · After breakfast, another half-day excursion (4 hours), through the lush Tijuca Forest, one of the largest urban forests in the world, home to an extraordinary variety of tropical flora and fauna, to the summit of Corcovado, where Christ the Redeemer overlooks the city. Named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, the monument offers breathtaking panoramic views of Rio, its famous beaches, mountains and Guanabara Bay.

The statue stands 710 metres above sea level. It is 38 metres tall and was built in 1931. From the viewing platform, you can see the Niterói Bridge, Guanabara Bay, the Botanical Garden, Maracanã Stadium, Sugar Loaf and other parts of the city.

In the afternoon, a 4-hour shared tour of Rocinha with an English-speaking guide is scheduled.

During the visit, the guide explains the origin of the word ‘favela’. According to this account, soldiers from Bahia fought royal troops on a hill where the favela tree grew. After the war, the survivors came to Rio de Janeiro to demand the pay they were owed and settled on Providência Hill. In memory of their former home, they began calling it Favela Hill.

The route then introduces you to everyday life in one of these neighbourhoods. Narrow streets climb the hillside, with open drainage channels alongside them, as well as homes, small shops and street stalls. Rio has around 700 favelas. People from many professions live here, including technicians and office workers. Rooms are rented out, and markets sell food and handicrafts. Life within the neighbourhood follows its own rules, and the streets differ markedly from the tourist districts by the ocean.

These neighbourhoods have their own internal rules. Visits require permission from the local ‘godfather’, and the police do not enter. The tour travels by jeep through Rocinha before returning to the hotel.

blocks.text: Day 4 · After breakfast, transfer to Rio de Janeiro airport for your flight to Foz do Iguaçu, where your driver meets you for the transfer to your hotel. In the afternoon, discover the Brazilian side of the magnificent Iguazu Falls on a guided tour: scenic walkways along the canyon offer spectacular views of countless cascades surrounded by lush Atlantic rainforest, culminating at the impressive Devil’s Throat, where you feel the power of the water and admire the rainbows in the spray. Recommended optional activities: a thrilling Macuco Safari boat adventure or a visit to the colourful Bird Park.
